Sponsored by



Evan Vucci/Reuters



Federal Reserve Gov. Michael Barr said further rate increases are likely needed  to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion. [https://www.wsj.com/pro/central-banking/feds-barr-says-more-rate-hikes-likely-needed-to-return-inflation-to-target-c165cb26]

Barr expressed that he supported the Fed’s decision to raise interest rates by a quarter-percentage point last week, speaking at an event in Chicago. He noted that risks to achieving the Fed’s inflation target have risen.

“Inflation is above our 2 percent target and not clearly trending toward target in a timely way,” a published text of his remarks said. “In my base case, further policy adjustments are likely to be needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion.”

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

Planning & Investing               Gadgets Are Going Premium—and Manufacturers Are Raking It In

Even as unit shipments fall, analysts expect device revenue to climb this year for smartphone players Samsung Electronics and Apple as  well as PC makers Lenovo, Dell Technologies. [https://www.wsj.com/tech/gadgets-are-going-premiumand-manufacturers-are-raking-it-in-2fa1130e]

Market Talk               

From  Dow Jones Newswires [https://www.dowjones.com/professional/newswires/]



The big players in buying exports of U.S. agricultural commodities right now include Canada, Mexico, and China -- but none of these markets are expected to grow much from where they are now, says the Farm Journal Foundation in a research note. So to support the increasing output of American farmers, the U.S. will need to nurture relationships with new buyers, says the organization. These new buyers would be in 'emerging markets' such as Africa and South Asia, developing areas that have the potential to expand exponentially and need the food supply to support that expansion. "The U.S. will need to rely on new, potentially rapidly growing markets to build its demand base and protect American farm livelihoods," says the Farm Journal Foundation. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)

Jefferies says it sees the Board of Trade as "the single possible deliverable," from the summit between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi. Agreed in May, the mechanism cuts tariffs toward most-favored-nation levels on $30 billion of goods in each direction, scoped to non-sensitive items, the analysts say in a note. They are optimistic that Board of Trade will be emphasized as a win by both sides because they say it's the only item that doesn't concede anything strategic. "Everything else runs into incentives neither leader will override before November. Taiwan, Japan, Iran and the Russia sanctions bill stay unresolved but set the risk backdrop." (patrick.sheridan@wsj.com)

Barron's Advisor               Market Strategist Julie Biel: The AI Craze Is Making These Quality Stocks More Affordable

Kayne Anderson Rudnick’s chief market strategist, Julie Biel, says investors’ rush to own big AI names  has left some great industrial and financial stocks underpriced. [https://www.barrons.com/advisor/articles/ai-stocks-investing-software-saas-4e61c2c1?mod=features]

Business & Practice               YouTube Is Battling Netflix Over Top Talent

Google-owned platform rolling out better tools for digital producers that could help it  keep more of their content exclusively. [https://www.wsj.com/business/media/youtube-is-battling-netflix-over-top-talent-eebbf0cf]

Impact Investing               McDonald’s Pledges Multibillion-Dollar Investment to Help Franchisees

The fast-food giant’s strategy aims to tackle rising costs, overhaul equipment  and expand market share in chicken and beverages. [https://www.wsj.com/business/hospitality/mcdonalds-pledges-multibillion-dollar-investment-to-help-franchisees-0fd2677e]

Talking Points               Trump’s Oil Allies Fear Losing Battle in Bid to Stop Diesel-Export Ban

American oil companies are fiercely opposed to the president’s nascent plan,  but vulnerable Republicans are putting pressure on him. [https://www.wsj.com/business/energy-oil/trumps-oil-allies-see-nightmare-scenario-of-diesel-export-ban-becoming-reality-16973ae2?mod=business_lead_pos2]

Travel & Lifestyle               The High-Stakes Pursuit of Smuggling Butter Home From Paris            

Elena Vardon/WSJ



Artisanal butter has become the must-have souvenir from France, but getting it back in one piece  can be a high-wire act. [https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/travel/the-high-stakes-pursuit-of-smuggling-butter-home-from-paris-fa4cee4c]
